# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### Request-volume collapse on CloudFront EEXAMPLE000001 (example-shop UI)
**Description:** On CloudFront distribution EEXAMPLE000001 (example-shop UI), request volume collapsed ~90% during 16:00–16:30 UTC on 2026-10-11 (steady ~11,100 req/5min baseline → trough of 963 at 16:15, ~91% below baseline). 4xxErrorRate stayed flat at 0% throughout and 5xx was ~0% (one trivial 0.13% blip at 16:05) — a request-volume collapse with near-zero errors, the signature of connection failures/timeouts where requests never complete. FULL RECOVERY at the 16:30 bucket (back to 11,038), holding ~10,700–11,400 through 17:10.
**Time:** 2026-10-11T16:00:00Z - 2026-10-11T16:30:00Z

## Findings

### Hypothesis: AWS WAF is not the cause of the incident
**Description:** WAF is being ruled out: zero BlockedRequests on the affected distribution's web ACL (CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4), no WAF/CloudFront configuration change in the window, and a symptom signature (request-volume collapse with near-zero error rate) that is inconsistent with a WAF block (which produces HTTP 403/4xx). WAF's own AllowedRequests dipped with the traffic, confirming it merely saw less traffic rather than suppressing it. Held as a hypothesis pending the origin (EKS us-west-2) examination.
